gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could open states that the Anker SOLIX S5000 publishes only an 8,000 W peak (33.3 A at 240 V by arithmetic) with no locked-rotor amp rating or peak duration; the core mechanism itself (pump locked-rotor amps against the inverter's current limit) is already on two of the results.
standout_why: I opened willitrunpower.com (rank 10), wellwaterauthority.com (rank 13) and homebatteryreport.com (rank 15). willitrunpower already gives Franklin's 230 V locked-rotor amps for 2-wire and 3-wire motors, the 65% start-voltage rule, the 50%-larger rule for 2-wire motors, and surge amps for the DELTA Pro 3 (33.3 A) and F3800 (37.5 A). homebatteryreport already gives the Franklin 2-wire table, says an inverter trips on current rather than watts, and quotes Anker's guide that the F3800 Plus LRA is 80 A. wellwaterauthority has only a 2-3x running-watts rule. None of the three mentions the Anker SOLIX S5000, and willitrunpower and wellwaterauthority do not mention NEMA code letters. offsprig.com (rank 1) and grid.ceo (rank 14) failed with a certificate error, so I did not compare against them. ChatGPT cited only EcoFlow's pages, which returned no readable content to me.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick, and it rests on rival-reported figures I could not verify in the primary documents. A conventional pressure-switch pump is gated by locked-rotor amps: by homebatteryreport's figures the F3800 Plus (80 A LRA) clears Franklin's 230 V 2-wire motors up to 1.5 HP (66.2 A), while 8,000 W-peak units such as the DELTA Pro 3 and the S5000 work out to 33.3 A, just above a 1/2 HP 2-wire (32.2 A) and below a 1 HP 2-wire (48.7 A). The one new point is that the S5000, despite a larger battery, has no published LRA and sits in the 8,000 W class on paper.

findings.label: Maker-stated AC output, peak and 240 V port
findings.value: 4,500 W continuous, 8,000 W peak, 120/240 V, L14-30R (also TT-30R and NEMA 5-20R); no LRA, peak duration, pump HP or price shown
findings.note: Read through a page-to-text fetch. My arithmetic: 8,000 W / 240 V = 33.3 A, assuming the peak is available across the 240 V port, which Anker does not state.

findings.label: Locked-rotor amp rating, second-hand
findings.value: 80 A LRA; soft starter advised for air conditioners needing more
findings.source_title: Battery backup for a well pump: the 240V and start-current problem | The Home Battery Report
findings.note: The Home Battery Report quotes Anker's user guide: 'The LRA (Locked Rotor Amps) of Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus is 80A'. I could not open the guide itself: the signaturesolar.com PDF came back as unreadable binary, and device.report and santansolar.com returned 403. This is a rival-page fact, not new.

findings.label: Franklin 3-wire locked-rotor amps and generator rules, second-hand
findings.value: 230 V 3-wire: 1/2 HP 23.0 A, 3/4 HP 34.2 A, 1 HP 41.8 A; source must hold at least 65% of rated voltage during start; 2-wire motors need a generator 50% larger
findings.source_title: Best power station for a well pump: 240 V, starting amps and what actually works | Willrun
findings.note: Willrun attributes these to Franklin and labels its station comparisons 'Paper estimate, not a bench test'. Primary document not opened by me. This is a rival-page fact, not new.

findings.value: 8,000 W surge, about 33.3 A; 4,000 W continuous; 4,096 Wh
